items.title: Buckingham interviewed by Monk Rowe, 2019
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] ...I heard the L.A. Juggernaut Big Band, Frankie Capp and Nat Pierce.

ctx.x: No, this morning in the class, this jazz class this morning, I was talking about recording. And I said when I started recording it was on 4-track. These guys were doing mono of course on disk and even when tape started it was mono. And then 2-track and eventually 3-track, then 4-track. I started in ’69 on 4-track, and then we’d go to Philadelphia, George Massenburg, my oldest friend in the business who is the man. He invented parametric equalization and all this stuff. We’re still friends. But George and I would…

Well that’s why when I listen to the Basie, they call it the All American Rhythm Section, it just sounds like one entity. Because they, I don’t know if they were so totally conscious of balancing their own volume but they surely did. And I had the experience once, on multiple, this one night after the other at a festival I heard the L.A. Juggernaut Big Band, Frankie Capp and Nat Pierce. And they had mics all over the place and it blew your head off. The next night the Count Basie Orchestra led by Grover Mitchell…
Frank Foster. At any rate they had like three mics on stage. And it was so much better. The band was in control rather than —
